newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda-Sudan peace talks hit deadlock.
newsitem.headline: Uganda-Sudan peace talks hit deadlock.

text.p: Iranian-sponsored peace talks between Uganda and Sudan hit a deadlock on Saturday when the two African countries failed to agree on a joint statement.
"The talks have failed but they have not completely failed. There is still room for negotiations," said Eriya Kategaya, Uganda's foreign minister and deputy prime minister.

He said Sudan refused to include in the statement a clause about Ugandan schoolchildren allegedly abducted in February by the rebel Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) and held at a camp at Arnu in southern Sudan.
"Our main concern was the violation of human rights especially the abduction of the 26 girls from the St Mary's College Aboke who are being held in Arnu," Kategaya added.

Doubts about the success of the talks now in their ninth round surfaced at their outset on Friday after Sudan sent only its first undersecretary in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to the Kampala talks.
There was no comment from the Sudanese representative.

Relations between the two countries are strained over accusations that Sudan is helping the rebel LRA in northern Uganda and that Uganda is supporting the rebel Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) in southern Sudan.
Uganda denied on Monday accusations by Khartoum that it had attacked two southern Sudanese border towns in support of the SPLA rebels fighting the Sudanese government.
Kampala accused Sudanese government warplanes of bombing northern Uganda in February but Khartoum denied doing so.
Uganda asked Iran to mediate last year when President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani visited Kampala.

Iran mediated an agreement between the two countries last September under which Uganda and Sudan agreed to resume diplomatic relations severed in April 1995 after an incident in which Sudanese diplomats refused to surrender a cache of weapons to Ugandan soldiers.
